He used to sell those through  advertisements and websites.
It is alleged that the accused  Mahesh and Deepakumar @ Amitkumar transacted business  with the informant.
Initially they made payments regularly  and subsequently took away more quantity but did not make  the payments.
The accused cheated the first informant for  the amount of Rs.56,32,540/-.
The investigation was carried  out and during investigation about 250 bags of cashew nuts  were recovered.

After that there was no progress in the trial and  the accused were continuously remaining absent.
According  to learned counsel for the Applicant, they are absconding.
In  the meantime, the original informant passed away.
The legal  heirs of the informant, the Petitioners herein, made an  application before the learned Magistrate for modifying that  particular condition of furnishing the bank guarantee.
Learned Magistrate rejected that application on the ground  that the condition was imposed pursuant to the order passed  by the Sessions Court.
Said order dated 27.6.2023 was  challenged by the Petitioners before the Sessions Court at  Kolhapur vide Criminal Revision Application No.71/2023.
That Revision Application was dismissed by this Court.
The  Petitioners then approached this Court.

sentences.text: 9. Learned APP expressed apprehension that during  trial if the Petitioners do not produce the amount then there  will be legal implication and complications.
10. I have considered these submissions.
The  accused are absconding.
The trial is not progressing further.
The bank guarantee is kept pending for a number of years  nor the informant nor his legal heirs were able to use that  amount.
In this case even as per the prosecution case the  informant was the victim and his case was genuine.
The  cashew nuts which were recovered during the investigation  were perishable and were permitted to be sold.

Therefore,
 there is no reason as to why the legal heirs of the informant  5 of 6 ::: Uploaded on - 19/06/2024 ::: Downloaded on - 25/06/2024 03:57:47 :::
 :6: 8.WP-ST-20184-23.odt  should suffer any further.
The conclusion of the trial is not  in sight.
The accused were absconding.
Therefore, the  condition of furnishing the bank guarantee after efflux of  time is onerous and unwarranted.
It would be sufficient if  the Petitioners execute an indemnity bond and undertake to  produce the amount in question before the trial Court if  necessary in future.
